review.verdict: Clean one-cycle run: all four workflows built and all 10 done-when items held with no refusals or redirects, but the full 50 budget was spent and one known defect shipped because no money was left to fix it.

identity.note: Recorded the charter without questions, which the placeholder rule justified [2]. Declared done and disclosed the defect once [23]. It never asked the Requester about a small budget raise, and its claim that the defect 'disappears' once a send channel is given is unverified.

adaptation.note: Asked for a counter instead of cutting the gallery or farms [4], and accepted explicitly with the risk stated [6]. It set the build order in [4] and [6], which is Coordination's job.

priority.note: Countered with named cuts, kept full scope at 50/50, and predicted the exact trade-off: no money for an 8 fix [5]. It checked every envelope [9][12][15][18]. Zero reserve was its own choice.

coordination.note: Correct dependency and file-lock reasoning, 0 holds [8][11][14][17]. Order was forced by one shared file, so the role was barely tested. It repeats the same rule text each turn, and [17] does not start with @name.

audit.note: Gave the cause (`.btn{display:inline-block}` overriding `hidden`), the fix cost, and labeled the browser check as unconfirmed [22]. Routing to Identity fits the 'may be done' hand-off.

builder.note: Four workflows built in four turns, each within its slot [10][13][16][19]. No JS errors, no overflow, 34 KB [21]. It shipped the hidden-button bug in the pre-order feature without flagging it.

went_well: Priority's counter [5] kept both the gallery and the farm stories at exactly 50/50, and Adaptation accepted in 2 attempts [6], with no Identity escalation.
Envelope check before every build, 0 holds, 0 redirects, 0 invalid moves, 0 validator refusals.
Code check [21]: no horizontal overflow at 360px or 1280px, no JS errors, no broken in-page links.
The placeholder rule handled missing facts with zero Requester questions, and the open inputs were listed once at the end [23].
Audit's unconfirmed caveat was passed to the Requester rather than dropped [23].
problems: Zero reserve and retry_limit 0 [5] left the one-line CSS fix (cost 8) unfunded [22]. Metrics show cap 100 and no raises, and nobody asked the Requester for more. Whether the agents could see the cap is not in the log.
The defect sits in the Send button of the pre-order, the core feature (done-when item 5). The mechanical check [21] missed it, and Audit had no browser to confirm it.

Charged equals agent_estimate for all four workflows, so spend is a rate card, not a measurement. The cuts in [5] (drop the styling part, price W2 as interactive_feature) fit the budget, with no evidence they were real savings.
Evidence is thin on Identity rulings, Coordination holds, REFUSE paths and validator rejections: 1 cycle, 0 conflicts reaching Identity, 0 Requester questions.
Adaptation and Coordination gave the same order [4][8], so independent scheduling cannot be confirmed.
learnings: Test a reserve: hold back about 10% (5 of 50), or let Priority request a raise from the Requester. Evidence: [5] and [22]. Cost: a slightly thinner scope.
Next run: make the budget cap visible and see whether Identity asks the Requester for a small raise instead of closing with a known defect.

Harness: add a mechanical check that flags any element with the hidden attribute whose computed display is not none. It would have caught F-5 [22]. Add a pre-order click-through check too, since done-when checks presence, not behavior.
Harness: log real calls or tokens next to the rate-card charge so estimate accuracy can be judged. Today all four match exactly.

To stress the design, run a budget below the cheapest viable scope (about 30) to force REFUSE, park and Identity rulings, and a vaguer brief to force Requester questions. This run cannot speak to those paths.

Keep: placeholders plus lazy loading kept both gallery and farms in scope at low cost, and the Audit-to-Identity 'may be done' path worked. Track audit warnings separately, since all_pass was true with a warning on a core feature.
